To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the transition probability estimates can help predict the future health status of older adults.

(1) older adults are likely to be in same health state 1 year later but a substantial proportion change in both directions, (2) the probabilities vary by initial health state and age, (3) men are more likely to transition to excellent health or dead and women to good or fair, (4) women will live longer but a higher proportion of their remaining years will be unhealthy,

the probabilities of transition in self-rated health states vary by initial health state (i.e., health state at the beginning of the interval), age, and sex; that men are more likely than women (and women are more likely than men) to transition to excellent and to dead, respectively; that women are more likely to transition to good and fair than men; and that women will have more healthy years of life, more unhealthy years of life, and a slightly higher proportion of remaining life healthy than men
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the health of older persons varies with age, sex, race, and socioeconomic status, and how these variations are related to health behaviors and to the health care system.
understanding the determinants of health in older adults.
the development and evaluation of methods of predicting the health of individuals or cohorts.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the transition probabilities estimated in this study are useful for predicting future health for older adults.

the probabilities of transition in self-rated health vary by age and by sex, that women have more remaining life than men, but that the proportion of that life that is healthy may be slightly higher in men, and that these estimates can be used for prediction.
the transition probabilities are not constant, and they do vary with age and sex.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the probability of remaining in the same health category is high but not perfect, and that transition probabilities are higher for persons who are in poor or dead categories, and higher for women than for men.
older adults are likely to have a substantial amount of healthy life remaining and that this amount is greater for men than for women.
older adults are most likely to be healthy 2 years later but that the proportion with poor health also increases, and the proportion with good and fair health declines.
The main takeaway from our work is that
transition probabilities are a key component in the calculation of healthy life expectancy (HLE).
self-rated health is a valid and useful predictor of future health, but not as good as a gold standard such as mortality.
it is important to take into account the health of older persons when projecting the health of the population.
